1.heading: The risen Jesus promises the Spirit and commissions witnesses
1.note: Over forty days he speaks about God's Kingdom; told to wait in Jerusalem, they ask about the kingdom, and he says they will be his witnesses

1.heading: Jesus departs and the apostles return to Jerusalem
1.note: He is taken up as they watch; two men in white speak, and the apostles pray in the upper room

1.heading: Peter interprets Judas's vacancy and Matthias is chosen
1.note: Peter speaks to about one hundred twenty; two men are put forward, they pray, and the lot falls on Matthias

2.heading: The Spirit fills the gathered disciples and languages cross boundaries
2.note: Wind-sound fills the house, tongues like fire sit on each of them, and visitors hear their own languages; others say 'new wine'

2.heading: Peter explains Pentecost and proclaims the risen Messiah
2.note: Peter says they are not drunk, since it is the third hour; he cites Joel and David, and says God raised the crucified Jesus

2.heading: Hearers respond and a shared community takes shape
2.note: Peter answers 'Repent and be baptized'; about three thousand are added that day, sharing goods and breaking bread at home

3.heading: A man unable to walk is healed in Jesus's name
3.note: At the Beautiful gate Peter says 'I have no silver or gold'; the lame beggar walks and leaps into the temple praising God

3.heading: Peter redirects the astonished crowd from the apostles to Israel's God
3.note: The healed man clings to Peter and John in Solomon's porch; Peter says it was not their power, and names Jesus, whom they denied

3.heading: Peter calls Israel to turn within the prophets' promise
3.note: Peter says they acted in ignorance; he cites Moses and Abraham's offspring, and says God sent his servant to them first

4.heading: The authorities arrest the witnesses and the community grows
4.note: Priests, the temple captain and Sadducees, upset at the teaching about resurrection, hold them overnight; about five thousand men believe

4.heading: Peter testifies before the council and the witnesses refuse silence
4.note: Rulers ask by what name; Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, names Jesus and the rejected stone, and the rulers threaten them

4.heading: The released community prays, receives boldness, and shares possessions
4.note: They pray about the rage against God's servant Jesus, the place shakes, and all speak boldly; owners lay land proceeds at the apostles' feet

5.heading: Ananias and Sapphira lie about a voluntary gift and die
5.note: Ananias and Sapphira keep back part of the price; Peter says they lied to God, and each falls dead and is buried

5.heading: Signs multiply and the imprisoned apostles return to the temple
5.note: The sick are laid in the streets for Peter's shadow; the high priest jails the apostles, but an angel opens the doors at night

5.heading: The council hears the witnesses, Gamaliel intervenes, and teaching continues
5.note: The high priest says they were forbidden to teach; Peter says they must obey God; Gamaliel urges leaving them alone, and they keep teaching

6.heading: A distribution inequity emerges between Hellenists and Hebrews
6.note: The Hellenists complain that their widows are neglected in the daily service; the twelve gather the disciples and say they should not serve tables

6.heading: The community chooses and commissions the Seven
6.note: Seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom are chosen, Stephen among them; prayer and laying on of hands follow, and many priests obey

6.heading: Stephen's signs and wisdom provoke charges before the council
6.note: Stephen works wonders; synagogue men dispute with him, false witnesses speak against the holy place, and his face looks like an angel's

7.heading: Abraham, Joseph, and God's presence before the temple
7.note: Asked 'Are these things so?', Stephen starts with God calling Abraham out of Mesopotamia, then Joseph, sold by his brothers, made governor over Egypt

7.heading: Moses is rejected, commissioned, and rejected again
7.note: Moses is raised by Pharaoh's daughter, flees after striking an Egyptian, hears God at the bush; the fathers later make a calf

7.heading: Tabernacle and temple yield to God's uncontained presence
7.note: The fathers carry the tabernacle in with Joshua; Solomon builds a house, yet God says 'heaven is my throne'

7.heading: Stephen accuses the council and dies as a Spirit-filled witness
7.note: He calls them stiff-necked, sees Jesus standing at God's right hand, and is stoned while calling 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit'

8.heading: Persecution scatters believers and Philip proclaims in Samaria
8.note: Saul ravages the assembly and the scattered believers preach; Philip proclaims Christ in Samaria with signs, and Simon the sorcerer believes and is baptized

8.heading: Peter and John confirm Samaritan inclusion and rebuke Simon
8.note: Peter and John lay hands on them and they receive the Spirit; Simon offers money, and Peter says 'May your silver perish with you'

8.heading: Philip interprets Isaiah, baptizes an Ethiopian official, and travels onward
8.note: On the Gaza road Philip finds a man of Ethiopia reading Isaiah, tells him about Jesus, and baptizes him; the Spirit catches Philip away

9.heading: The risen Jesus stops Saul and Ananias receives him
9.note: A light and a voice stop Saul; blind three days, he receives sight when Ananias lays hands on him, and is baptized

9.heading: Saul proclaims Jesus, escapes plots, and is welcomed through Barnabas
9.note: Saul preaches in the synagogues; the Jews plot to kill him, disciples lower him in a basket, and Barnabas brings him to the apostles

9.heading: Peter heals Aeneas and restores Tabitha at Joppa
9.note: Peter tells Aeneas, bedridden eight years, to get up; at Joppa he sends everyone out, prays, and says 'Tabitha, get up'

10.heading: Cornelius receives a vision and sends for Peter
10.note: Cornelius, a centurion who prays and gives to the needy, sees an angel and sends two servants and a soldier to Joppa

10.heading: Peter's vision and the Spirit prepare him to cross the threshold
10.note: Hungry on the housetop, Peter sees a sheet of animals let down three times; the Spirit tells him to go with the three men

10.heading: Peter enters Cornelius's house and reframes purity around people
10.note: Cornelius falls at Peter's feet and Peter raises him; Peter says God showed him to call no man unclean; Cornelius tells of the angel

10.heading: Peter proclaims Jesus and the Spirit falls before baptism
10.note: Peter says God shows no favoritism and tells of Jesus healing, killed on a tree, and raised; the Spirit falls on all who hear

11.heading: Peter defends Gentile table fellowship by recounting God's initiative
11.note: Those of the circumcision contend with Peter over eating with uncircumcised men; he retells the sheet and the Spirit falling, and they glorify God

11.heading: The scattered mission reaches Greeks and Barnabas strengthens Antioch
11.note: Men of Cyprus and Cyrene preach to the Hellenists in Antioch; Barnabas, sent from Jerusalem, brings Saul, and disciples are first called Christians

11.heading: Agabus predicts famine and Antioch sends relief to Judea
11.note: Agabus, one of the prophets from Jerusalem, says by the Spirit a great famine is coming; the disciples send relief by Barnabas and Saul

12.heading: Herod kills James and imprisons Peter while the church prays
12.note: Herod kills James, John's brother, with the sword; he arrests Peter and sets four squads of soldiers to guard him while the assembly prays

12.heading: An angel frees Peter and Rhoda announces him to the incredulous gathering
12.note: An angel wakes Peter in prison; at Mary's house Rhoda runs in without opening the gate, and they say 'You are crazy'

12.heading: Herod accepts divine acclaim, dies, and the word multiplies
12.note: In royal clothing Herod gives a speech; the people shout 'The voice of a god', an angel strikes him, and he dies

13.heading: The Spirit sends Barnabas and Saul from Antioch
13.note: While the prophets and teachers fast and serve, the Spirit says to separate Barnabas and Saul; they fast, pray, and send them

13.heading: The missionaries cross Cyprus and confront Elymas
13.note: They sail to Cyprus; at Paphos the sorcerer Elymas opposes them, Paul says he will be blind, and the proconsul believes

13.heading: Paul proclaims Israel's fulfilled hope in Pisidian Antioch
13.note: Paul recounts Israel's story from Egypt to David, says God raised Jesus; the Gentiles ask that it be preached the next Sabbath

13.heading: Opposition and reception spread the word toward Gentiles
13.note: Almost the whole city gathers; the Jews contradict, Paul and Barnabas say they turn to the Gentiles, and they shake off the dust

14.heading: Mixed response and threatened violence divide Iconium
14.note: In Iconium many Jews and Greeks believe; others embitter the Gentiles, the city divides, and the apostles flee a plot to stone them

14.heading: A healing in Lystra is mistaken for a divine visitation
14.note: Paul tells a man who never walked to stand upright and he leaps up; the crowd calls Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercury

14.heading: Paul is stoned, the missionaries retrace their route, and elders are appointed
14.note: Jews from Antioch and Iconium win over the crowds and stone Paul, who rises and goes on; they appoint elders and return to Antioch

15.heading: Circumcision teachers provoke a journey to Jerusalem
15.note: Men from Judea teach that unless circumcised the brothers cannot be saved; Paul and Barnabas go to Jerusalem, where some Pharisees demand the law

15.heading: Peter, Barnabas, Paul, and James discern Gentile inclusion
15.note: Peter says God made no distinction; James cites the prophets and says to write that Gentiles abstain from idols, immorality, strangled things, and blood

15.heading: The assembly sends a letter and delegates to Antioch
15.note: The assembly sends Judas and Silas with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch with a letter; the brothers rejoice, and Judas and Silas encourage them

15.heading: Paul and Barnabas separate over John Mark
15.note: Paul wants to revisit the brothers; they quarrel over taking John Mark, Barnabas takes Mark to Cyprus, and Paul chooses Silas

16.heading: Timothy joins and the Spirit redirects the team toward Macedonia
16.note: Paul circumcises Timothy; the Spirit forbids speaking in Asia, and a man of Macedonia in a vision begs 'Come over into Macedonia'

16.heading: Lydia receives the word and opens her household
16.note: At Philippi they speak to women by a river; Lydia, a seller of purple, listens as the Lord opens her heart; she is baptized

16.heading: Deliverance from a divining spirit provokes beating and prison
16.note: Paul commands a spirit out of a girl; her masters drag him and Silas to the magistrates, and they are beaten with rods

16.heading: The jailer and household believe; Roman abuse is exposed
16.note: An earthquake opens the doors; the jailer asks 'what must I do to be saved'; the magistrates, hearing they are Romans, beg them to leave

17.heading: Scriptural reasoning in Thessalonica provokes belief and civic charges
17.note: In Thessalonica Paul reasons three Sabbaths from the Scriptures; some join him, unpersuaded Jews raise a crowd, and they drag Jason before the rulers

17.heading: Bereans receive and examine the word amid renewed pressure
17.note: In Beroea they examine the Scriptures daily; Jews from Thessalonica come agitating the crowds, and the brothers send Paul to the sea

17.heading: Paul debates Athens and addresses the Areopagus
17.note: Paul speaks at the Areopagus of an altar 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD'; some mock the resurrection, while Dionysius and Damaris believe

18.heading: Paul works and witnesses with Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth
18.note: Paul works with Aquila and Priscilla; opposed in the synagogue, he turns to the Gentiles, and the Lord says he has many people there

18.heading: Gallio dismisses the synagogue opponents' case
18.note: The Jews bring Paul before Gallio, saying he persuades men to worship contrary to the law; Gallio drives them off, and Sosthenes is beaten

18.heading: Paul travels onward while Priscilla and Aquila teach Apollos
18.note: Paul leaves Priscilla and Aquila at Ephesus and sails on; the couple take Apollos aside and explain the way of God more accurately

19.heading: Twelve disciples receive fuller instruction, baptism, and the Spirit
19.note: About twelve men with only John's baptism are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus; Paul lays hands on them and they prophesy

19.heading: Daily teaching and extraordinary works spread the word through Asia
19.note: Three months in the synagogue, then daily in the school of Tyrannus; handkerchiefs and aprons from Paul's body are carried to the sick

19.heading: Failed magical use of Jesus's name leads to confession and renunciation
19.note: Sceva's seven sons invoke Jesus; the spirit answers 'Jesus I know, and Paul I know' and they flee wounded; many burn their magic books

19.heading: The Artemis economy erupts into a confused civic assembly
19.note: Demetrius the silversmith gathers the craftsmen; they cry 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians' until the town clerk dismisses the assembly

20.heading: A diverse team accompanies Paul's return through Macedonia
20.note: Paul goes through Macedonia to Greece and stays three months; a Jewish plot makes him return through Macedonia, with named companions

20.heading: Eutychus falls during the Troas gathering and is restored
20.note: Paul talks until midnight; Eutychus, asleep in the window, falls from the third floor, is taken up dead, and is brought in alive

20.heading: Paul travels to Miletus and rehearses his ministry
20.note: Paul calls the Ephesus elders to Miletus; he says bonds wait for him, and they will see his face no more

20.heading: Elders are charged to guard the flock, work, give, and remember
20.note: Paul warns of wolves, says 'more blessed to give', then kneels to pray; they weep, kiss him, and go with him to the ship

21.heading: Disciples and prophets warn Paul along the voyage
21.note: Disciples at Tyre tell Paul not to go up; Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul's belt; Paul is ready to die

21.heading: Jerusalem leaders receive Paul and propose public purification
21.note: James and the elders glorify God and tell Paul to purify himself with four men under a vow; he does so in the temple

21.heading: A false temple accusation provokes mob violence and Roman arrest
21.note: Jews from Asia seize Paul in the temple, claiming he brought Greeks in; the crowd beats him until the commanding officer arrests him

21.heading: Paul identifies himself and asks to address the crowd
21.note: The officer asks 'Do you know Greek' and takes Paul for the Egyptian; Paul says he is a Jew from Tarsus

22.heading: Paul establishes Jewish identity and recounts persecuting the Way
22.note: Paul speaks in Hebrew; he says he was born in Tarsus, taught at Gamaliel's feet, and persecuted the Way to the death

22.heading: Paul retells the Damascus encounter and Ananias's commission
22.note: Near Damascus a great light shines and a voice asks 'why are you persecuting me'; Ananias says to receive sight and be baptized

22.heading: A temple vision sends Paul to Gentiles and the crowd erupts
22.note: Paul says he was told to leave Jerusalem and be sent far to the Gentiles; the crowd shouts 'Rid the earth of this fellow'

22.heading: Roman citizenship prevents an unlawful flogging
22.note: Paul asks the centurion if it is lawful to scourge a Roman; the officer says he bought his citizenship, Paul was born a Roman

23.heading: A blow, rebuke, and resurrection claim divide the council
23.note: Ananias commands Paul struck on the mouth; Paul says he is a Pharisee judged over the resurrection, and Pharisees and Sadducees argue

23.heading: The Lord promises Roman witness and a murder conspiracy forms
23.note: The Lord says 'Cheer up, Paul' and that he must testify at Rome; over forty Jews bind themselves under a curse to kill him

23.heading: Paul's nephew exposes the plot through Roman channels
23.note: Paul's sister's son warns him of more than forty men lying in wait; a centurion brings the young man to the commanding officer

23.heading: A military transfer and self-protective letter send Paul to Felix
23.note: Soldiers take Paul by night to Antipatris and on to Caesarea with a letter; Felix says he will hear him when his accusers arrive

24.heading: Tertullus flatters Felix and accuses Paul of sedition and profanation
24.note: Tertullus praises Felix's foresight, then calls Paul 'a plague', a ringleader of the Nazarenes who tried to profane the temple; the Jews join in

24.heading: Paul denies the facts while confessing the Way and resurrection hope
24.note: Paul says they cannot prove the charges; he serves God according to the Way, and is judged concerning the resurrection of the dead

24.heading: Felix delays, fears Paul's ethical message, seeks a bribe, and leaves him bound
24.note: Felix puts the case off, is terrified at 'the judgment to come', hopes for money from Paul, and after two years leaves him bound

25.heading: Festus rejects a transfer plot and orders accusers to Caesarea
25.note: The high priest and principal men ask Festus to summon Paul, plotting to kill him on the way; Festus keeps him at Caesarea

25.heading: Paul denies unproved charges and appeals to Caesar
25.note: At Caesarea the Jews bring charges they cannot prove; Festus asks if Paul will be judged at Jerusalem; he says 'I appeal to Caesar'

25.heading: Festus explains the resurrection dispute to Agrippa
25.note: Festus tells Agrippa that the accusers had questions about their religion and about 'one Jesus', who was dead but Paul affirmed him alive

25.heading: Royal ceremony exposes the absence of clear charges
25.note: With great pomp Agrippa and Bernice enter; Festus says Paul did nothing worthy of death, and it seems unreasonable to send him without charges

26.heading: Paul locates his trial within Pharisaic resurrection hope
26.note: Agrippa lets Paul speak; Paul says he lived as a Pharisee and is judged for the hope of the promise to the fathers

26.heading: Paul confesses persecution and recounts Jesus's commission
26.note: Paul says he jailed saints; on the Damascus road at noon a light outshines the sun, and Jesus appoints him servant and witness

26.heading: Paul describes obedient repentance preaching and scriptural witness
26.note: Paul says he declared repentance from Damascus to the Gentiles, was seized in the temple, and says only what the prophets and Moses said

26.heading: Festus interrupts, Paul appeals to Agrippa, and the rulers affirm innocence
26.note: Festus shouts 'Paul, you are crazy'; Agrippa asks if Paul is making him a Christian; the rulers say he does nothing worthy of death

27.heading: The prisoners sail under Julius and reach Fair Havens with difficulty
27.note: The centurion Julius takes Paul and other prisoners by ship, treats Paul kindly at Sidon, and contrary winds slow them to Fair Havens

27.heading: Paul's warning is rejected and a northeaster overwhelms the ship
27.note: Paul warns of loss, but the centurion heeds the ship's master; a stormy wind drives them, and all hope of being saved is gone

27.heading: Paul announces preservation and prevents the sailors' escape
27.note: Paul says an angel stood by him and no life will be lost; when sailors try to flee, soldiers cut the boat's ropes

27.heading: All eat, the ship wrecks, and every person reaches land
27.note: Paul urges all to eat and breaks bread with thanks; the ship runs aground and the stern breaks up, but all reach land

28.heading: Malta's people welcome the survivors; Paul survives the viper and heals
28.note: Islanders light a fire in the rain; a viper fastens on Paul's hand, he shakes it into the fire, and he heals Publius's father

28.heading: The voyage reaches Italy and believers encourage Paul on the Appian Way
28.note: After three months they sail to Puteoli; brothers meet Paul, he thanks God, and in Rome he stays by himself with a soldier

28.heading: Paul explains his chain and Israel's hope to Roman Jewish leaders
28.note: Paul tells the Jewish leaders he did nothing against the people, appealed to Caesar, and is chained for Israel's hope

28.heading: A day-long scriptural witness ends in mixed response and unhindered teaching
28.note: Paul explains God's Kingdom from morning to evening; some believe and some disbelieve; he stays two years teaching 'without hindrance'

The reviewers' source quotations came through a page reader that returns short excerpts, and for some long pages a summary. The lead read every proposed edit and outline note but did not re-read the quotations.
Where a guide sentence names an ancient writer the reviewers did not read directly (for example Ovid, Suetonius or Augustine through a reference page), the `basis` says where the statement was read.

The Meta reader's subscription quota ran out partway through this book. A third outside model, `beam-free` through opencode, read the chapters it missed, after the main review; its findings that no claim already covered were checked in a late ledger.
Each reviewer was one pass with a stated bar ("a careful editor would ask: says who?"). A claim below that bar may remain.
Readings marked as readings were not adjudicated.
